stories.headline: Arson investigation underway at Fenland property
stories.brief: Police are investigating a suspected arson at a house in the Fens. The Cambs Times has released the first photograph of the property involved in the incident. No further details regarding the location or the circumstances of the fire have been provided at this stage.

stories.headline: Wisbech road reopens following water main repairs
stories.brief:
North End in Wisbech has reopened to traffic following the completion of repairs to a burst water main. The route had been closed for nearly a week, causing disruption for local businesses and road users after the issue was first reported to police last Thursday afternoon.

Anglian Water managed the repair work and has thanked residents for their patience during the closure. The company stated that the burst was likely caused by recent high temperatures, which can lead to ground movement and subsequent damage to pipes. The road is now fully accessible again.

stories.headline: MPs in disagreement over Cambridgeshire and Peterborough council plans
stories.brief: Members of Parliament are currently at odds regarding the future of council arrangements for Cambridgeshire and Peterborough. The proposed plans have sparked a clash between local representatives, though specific details of the disagreement remain limited. Residents across the Fens are advised that the debate concerns the long-term structure of local government in the region. We will continue to monitor the situation as further information regarding these council proposals becomes available.

stories.headline: Emergency services attend house fire in Lincolnshire village
stories.brief: Emergency crews are currently at the scene of a house fire in a Lincolnshire village. Details regarding the exact location of the property and the cause of the blaze have not yet been released. There is no information available at this time concerning potential casualties or the extent of the damage to the building. Emergency services remain in attendance as they deal with the incident. We will bring you further updates as more information becomes available.

stories.headline: Supermarket opening hours for August bank holiday
stories.brief: Shoppers across the Fens are being advised to check local opening times for major supermarkets this August bank holiday. Stores including Tesco, Aldi, Lidl, and Sainsbury’s are expected to operate on altered schedules over the long weekend. Customers are encouraged to verify the specific hours for their nearest branch before travelling, as opening times may vary by location. Further details regarding these changes are available through the Cambridge News website.

stories.headline: Wisbech man raises over £20,000 for hospice after Kilimanjaro climb
stories.brief:
A Wisbech man has successfully reached the summit of Mount Kilimanjaro, raising more than £20,780 for the hospice that cared for his late brother. Simon Chaplin completed the eight-day trek in memory of his brother, Richard, who passed away last December at the age of 49. 

Mr. Chaplin aimed to raise £17,991 for St Peter’s Hospice in Bristol, representing one pound for every day of his brother’s life. Despite facing freezing temperatures and difficult conditions during the climb, he reached the 19,341ft summit on August 16. Mr. Chaplin has thanked everyone who supported his fundraising efforts, noting that the experience has given him greater confidence in his own abilities.

stories.headline: Conservation work begins at King’s Lynn’s historic Custom House
stories.brief:
Conservation work has officially begun at the Custom House in King’s Lynn to preserve the Grade I listed building for the future. The project aims to restore the historic stonework, windows, and cupola while upgrading the interior to create a flexible, accessible space for the community. Planned improvements include a new platform lift and updated facilities, with further enhancements to the surrounding Purfleet Quay expected by spring 2027.

Originally commissioned in 1683 by Sir John Turner and designed by architect Henry Bell, the building served as a merchants' exchange before becoming a customs house. The council is now seeking old photographs or personal stories from residents to help document the landmark’s rich maritime history.

stories.headline: Roof collapse reported at Iceland supermarket
stories.brief: Reports have emerged that the roof of an Iceland supermarket has collapsed. The incident, which was covered by the BBC, involves the store premises. No further details regarding the location or any potential injuries have been provided at this time. Listeners are advised to avoid the area if they are nearby. We will bring you further updates on this story as more information becomes available.

stories.headline: Waterlees estate to host pop-up mini-festival this September
stories.brief:
The Waterlees estate in Wisbech is set to host the We Are Waterlees pop-up festival on Saturday, September 26. Organised by Marketplace Art, the event aims to celebrate the local community with a variety of activities, music, and food.

Attendees can enjoy performances from KJ Folk, including ceilidh dancing, alongside sports such as football, archery, and axe throwing provided by the Living Better team. The Youths of Fenland horsebox will be serving pizza, and musician and poet Jay Sandhu will lead a songwriting session. The festival is designed to showcase the creativity and talent of Waterlees residents, with opportunities for everyone to get involved throughout the day.

stories.headline: MPs debate Cambridgeshire council restructuring
stories.brief: Members of Parliament have held a debate in Westminster regarding proposed changes to the structure of local councils in Cambridgeshire. The discussion saw representatives express differing views on the potential reorganisation of local government services across the county. No further details regarding the specific nature of the restructuring or the outcome of the parliamentary session have been provided.

stories.headline: Man sentenced for prison-based burglary plot and driving offences
stories.brief: A man has been sentenced for orchestrating a burglary while serving time in a prison cell. Lincolnshire Police confirmed the individual was also convicted for a series of traffic-related offences. The sentencing follows an investigation into the man's activities both behind bars and on the road. No further details regarding the length of the sentence or the specific location of the burglary have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Wisbech homelessness charity secures £600,000 funding boost
stories.brief:
The Ferry Project in Wisbech has been awarded a £600,000 grant from the government-backed Ending Homelessness in Communities fund. The charity plans to use the money to focus on preventing homelessness through early intervention and tenancy support, alongside providing recovery pathways for those with complex needs. 

The initiative, developed alongside local partners including Fenland District Council and health services, aims to offer intensive support for individuals facing significant barriers to stable housing. CEO Sandra Ferreira says the funding will help provide lasting solutions for vulnerable people in the community. The project is scheduled to begin delivery between October and November.

stories.headline: Planned Nursery Lane closure suspended following safety concerns
stories.brief:
A planned two-day closure of Nursery Lane in the Woottons has been suspended at the last minute. The work, which was scheduled to begin this morning, was halted following concerns from residents and local councillors regarding road safety. 

The area is currently experiencing traffic disruption due to emergency gas repairs being carried out by Cadent on Castle Rising Road. Officials from Norfolk County Council confirmed the Nursery Lane maintenance has been delayed until the emergency works on Castle Rising Road are finished. The decision follows criticism from councillors Simon Ring and Paul Bland, who raised fears that the simultaneous closures would force motorists onto an unsafe diversion route via the A149.

stories.headline: Wisbech fan pays tribute following death of Dolly Parton
stories.brief: A Wisbech man has shared his memories of meeting Dolly Parton following the news of the singer’s death this week at the age of 80. Michael Creed, a long-time admirer of the American star, first met her backstage at London’s Hammersmith Apollo in 2002. Mr. Creed, who co-founded a UK fan newsletter in the late 1990s, later met the icon again during a television appearance. He described the singer as a down-to-earth person who made time for her supporters. Mr. Creed, who has collected extensive memorabilia of the artist since 1974, said he was in shock following the announcement of her passing.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn charity secures funding to support veterans
stories.brief:
A King’s Lynn-based charity, The Bridge for Heroes, has received a funding boost from the Veterans’ Foundation. The grant will allow the South Clough Lane organisation to expand its welfare services for serving personnel, veterans, and their families. 

The charity aims to use the money to reduce isolation, anxiety, and stress within the Armed Forces community by providing accessible, person-centred support. CEO Helen Taylor says the funding will help the team reach more people in need. Anyone from the Armed Forces community seeking assistance or someone to talk to can contact the charity on 01553 760 230.

stories.headline: Teenage motorcyclist dies following Peterborough collision
stories.brief: A teenage motorcyclist has died following a head-on collision in Peterborough. The incident, which involved the motorcyclist, has been reported by the BBC. No further details regarding the exact location or the circumstances of the crash have been released at this time. Police are expected to provide more information as their inquiries continue.

stories.headline: Changes announced for Cambridgeshire bus timetables
stories.brief: Passengers across Cambridgeshire are being advised of upcoming changes to local bus services. A shake-up of current timetables has been announced, which will affect routes throughout the county. Commuters and regular travellers are encouraged to check their specific service schedules to see how these adjustments may impact their journeys. Further details regarding the revised timings are expected to be made available by local transport providers.

stories.headline: Students protest toilet policy at University Academy Long Sutton
stories.brief: Pupils at University Academy Long Sutton have staged a protest regarding changes to the school's toilet regulations. The demonstration follows the introduction of new rules concerning student access to facilities at the site. No further details regarding the specific nature of the policy changes or the outcome of the protest have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: Two new biogas projects launched in Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: Pretoria Energy has announced the launch of two new biogas projects within Cambridgeshire. The company confirmed the development as part of its latest expansion in the region. Further details regarding the specific locations or the operational capacity of these new sites have not yet been released.

stories.headline: New film The Dog Stars now showing at The Light in Wisbech
stories.brief: The film The Dog Stars is currently showing at The Light cinema in Wisbech. The post-apocalyptic drama features performances from Jacob Elordi, Margaret Qualley, Josh Brolin, and Guy Pearce. Set thirty years after a global pandemic, the story follows a mechanic named Hig who leaves his survival compound in search of a mysterious radio signal. While the film is described as a dark and brooding survival tale, reviewers suggest that a confusing sequence in the final hour prevents it from reaching its full potential. Despite this, the production offers a satisfying conclusion for local cinema-goers.

stories.headline: Local charity fundraiser success and upcoming events
stories.brief:
A recent charity yard sale held on Sunday, August 23, has raised £330 for Macmillan Cancer Support. Organisers expressed their gratitude to the community for the donations and support received. Following this success, the group plans to participate in the Terrington St Clement village yard sale on Saturday, September 26, between 10am and 2pm at 19 Eastgate Lane.

Elsewhere, the Norfolk Goldwings group will be in New Conduit Street this Saturday. Members will be displaying their Honda Goldwing motorbikes and trikes to collect funds for the East Anglian Air Ambulance. Residents are invited to attend and support the cause.

stories.headline: Wisbech youngster completes 93-mile charity walk
stories.brief:
An 11-year-old from Wisbech has raised over £3,200 for local charities after completing a 93-mile walk. Shyla Brown, a pupil at Peckover Primary School, walked from Silverstone race track to the Alan Hudson Centre in Wisbech over three days. Accompanied by Darren Barnard, she took more than 185,000 steps to honour the memory of Emma Barnard. 

The funds raised will support the Alan Hudson Centre and Edith’s Purse, a charity providing aid to families in poverty. Shyla was greeted by the Mayor of Wisbech, Lucie Foice-Beard, as she completed the final leg of her journey on Sunday afternoon. Donations are still being accepted following the successful challenge.

stories.headline: Bereavement services open day at Mintlyn Crematorium
stories.brief:
Mintlyn Crematorium in Bawsey is hosting a community open day on Saturday, September 12. Running from 9.30am until 1pm, the event offers families the chance to explore the grounds and learn about the cremation process. Staff will provide regular tours and talks, while various local funeral professionals and bereavement support services will be on hand to offer guidance.

Visitors are invited to ask questions in a supportive environment and view the Book of Remembrance Room. The event will also raise funds for local charities, including Tapping House hospice and the 8:56 Foundation. Any donations made during the morning will be shared between these causes.

stories.headline: Peterborough Cathedral displays new needlework project
stories.brief: Peterborough Cathedral has unveiled a new artistic tribute to its historic medieval ceiling. The project features the cathedral's famous ceiling recreated in needlework, consisting of one and a half million individual stitches. The Association of English Cathedrals confirmed the completion of the work, which highlights the intricate design of the landmark's interior. Visitors to the city can now view the detailed textile display at the cathedral.

stories.headline: Planning permission granted for East Cambridgeshire industrial site
stories.brief: Planning permission has been granted for an industrial site in East Cambridgeshire. The approval follows a long-running dispute regarding the development. No further details have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Lincolnshire village identified as one of the country's most deprived areas
stories.brief: A village in Lincolnshire has been highlighted as one of the most deprived locations in the UK. According to a report by LincsOnline, the area has been described as a "forgotten" community. The findings place the village among the most disadvantaged regions across the country. No further details regarding the specific location or the criteria used for the assessment have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire County Council considers school parking cameras
stories.brief:
Cambridgeshire County Council is exploring the use of cameras outside schools to tackle illegal and dangerous parking. The authority’s highways and transport committee is reviewing a report on how camera technology could enforce traffic rules and support ‘school streets’ schemes, which restrict vehicle access during drop-off and pick-up times.

While councillors have welcomed the proposal, committee chair Alex Beckett noted that volunteers remain vital to the success of these zones. However, officials acknowledged that cameras may be necessary in areas where volunteers have faced harassment. Any implementation of these measures will require further assessment before receiving final approval.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn coffee shop reopens drive-thru following ram raid
stories.brief:
The Costa Coffee branch at St Nicholas Retail Park in King’s Lynn has reopened for drive-thru and delivery customers following a ram raid last week. The store on Edward Benefer Way was forced to close after a stolen car was driven into the building at 2:51am last Thursday. The incident caused significant damage to the main entrance, which has now been boarded up.

While the drive-thru lane is operational, the shop remains closed to walk-in customers. Norfolk Police confirmed that the stolen vehicle used in the raid has been recovered, though no arrests have been made at this stage. It is not yet known when the premises will fully reopen for sit-in service.

stories.headline: Drainage works to cause disruption on A149 near King’s Lynn
stories.brief:
Drivers in the King’s Lynn area should prepare for delays starting September 21. Norfolk County Council is beginning a six-week project to upgrade drainage systems along the A149 Queen Elizabeth Way. 

To allow for the work, two-way traffic lights will be in operation overnight between 7pm and 6am, Monday to Friday. Additionally, a reduced speed limit of 30mph and 40mph will be enforced around the clock across a 1.2-kilometre stretch. The project, which costs £105,000, will focus on the verge on the east side of the carriageway, beginning 280 metres north-east of the Gaywood River bridge. Motorists are advised to plan their journeys accordingly while these essential improvements are carried out.

stories.headline: Residents urged to share views on West Norfolk housing plans
stories.brief:
West Norfolk Council has launched a public consultation regarding the future of the borough, as it plans for 8,500 new homes over the next 15 years. The initiative, titled People, Opportunities, Places, aims to address housing demand while also considering infrastructure, employment, and medical facilities.

Residents are invited to comment on suggested sites or propose new locations for development. The consultation is open until midnight on Tuesday, September 29. The council is hosting several in-person drop-in sessions and online events to gather feedback. Further details and survey forms are available on the West Norfolk Council website or at their King’s Court offices in King’s Lynn.

stories.headline: Gaywood man convicted of sexual assault
stories.brief:
A 37-year-old man from Gaywood has been found guilty of sexual assault. Sean Flanagan, of Bagge Road, appeared at King’s Lynn Magistrates’ Court yesterday for a summary trial. He was convicted of touching a woman aged 16 or over without her consent during an incident on November 18, 2025. 

The court has adjourned the case to allow for the preparation of a pre-sentence report. Mr Flanagan has been released on bail and is due to return to the same court on November 5 to be sentenced. Legal restrictions remain in place regarding the identification of individuals involved in the case.

stories.headline: Future of key services at Queen Elizabeth Hospital under discussion
stories.brief:
Senior leaders at the Norfolk and Waveney University Hospitals Group are discussing the potential closure of accident and emergency, intensive care, and maternity units at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn. The group is developing a long-term strategy for the county’s hospitals, though they insist no final decisions have been made. 

Officials state that any changes would require clinical evidence and formal public consultation. While the group maintains that urgent and emergency care will remain available at the site, this could involve scaled-down services. Local MPs have expressed differing views on the proposals, with calls for urgent reassurance regarding the hospital's future status. The facility is currently part of a planned 1.4 billion pound rebuild project.

stories.headline: Looking back at a Tudor-themed start for King’s Lynn pupils
stories.brief:
We are taking a trip down memory lane to September 2013, when pupils at Gaywood Community Primary School in King’s Lynn began their autumn term with a historical twist. To encourage curiosity and engagement from the very first day, staff decorated classrooms and introduced themed costumes for the students.

Year Four children embraced the new school year by dressing in Tudor attire. Headteacher Paul Shanks explained that the initiative was designed to provide a memorable start to the term, prompting students to ask questions and immerse themselves in their learning immediately. The project featured teacher Camilla Ridley alongside pupils Ellie-May Gotsell, Oscar Thomson, Claudia Draper, and Kieran O’Donnell.

stories.headline: Hospital team to tackle 180-mile challenge for new scanner
stories.brief: A spinal surgery team from Norfolk and Norwich University Hospitals is preparing for a six-day fundraising event to purchase a new EOS imaging system. Starting on Friday, September 4, the "Spineathlon 2026" will see the team kayak, walk, and cycle 180 miles across the region. Their route includes stops in Holkham, Hunstanton, and King’s Lynn. The appeal aims to raise the remaining funds for the £841,000 scanner, which provides accurate spinal images for children with scoliosis while reducing radiation exposure by 80 percent. So far, £660,000 has been collected through donations. The team will conclude their journey by cycling from the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn back to Norwich.

stories.headline: Looking back at West Norfolk history and recent local developments
stories.brief:
This week’s look back at local history highlights the 25th anniversary celebrations of the Downham and District Flower Club, held in September 1986. Also featured is a 2014 visit by the Duke and Duchess of Cambridge, who enjoyed a meal at the King’s Head Hotel in Great Bircham.

In more recent news, West Norfolk residents are preparing for an expanded recycling scheme starting next month, allowing more plastics and cartons to be placed in green bins. Meanwhile, Southery Parish Council is campaigning for a village bypass to address concerns over heavy traffic, and West Norfolk Council has approved plans for new housing developments at two sites in Gaywood.

stories.headline: Concerns raised over potential service changes at Queen Elizabeth Hospital
stories.brief:
Politicians in West Norfolk have expressed alarm following reports that the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn could face a downgrade. Discussions are reportedly underway regarding the potential closure of the hospital’s Accident and Emergency, intensive care, and maternity units as part of a long-term strategy. 

Local councillors and campaigners have voiced strong opposition, warning that such moves would force patients to travel long distances for emergency care. However, the Norfolk and Waveney University Hospitals Group states that no decisions have been made. Chief executive Professor Lesley Dwyer confirmed that clinical experts are developing a long-term strategy, but stressed that the hospital will continue to provide 24-hour urgent and emergency care for the local community.

stories.headline: Queen Elizabeth Hospital apologises to patient over ward placement
stories.brief:
The Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn has issued an apology after a 79-year-old patient from Tilney St Lawrence reported feeling "frightened and unheard" during her stay last week. Jill Dewsbury, who was admitted with hip pain, claimed she was moved to a ward she believed was for dementia patients, leading her to accuse the hospital of ageist treatment. 

The hospital’s chief nurse, Dawn Collins, has apologised for the distress caused. The trust clarified that the West Dereham ward is not a dementia unit, but cares for older adults with various medical needs. The hospital confirmed it is now reviewing the formal complaint submitted by Mrs Dewsbury.

stories.headline: Looking back at West Norfolk community milestones
stories.brief:
We are taking a look back at local memories from across West Norfolk. In 2011, True’s Yard Museum in King’s Lynn hosted a special event focused on the experiences of wartime evacuees, featuring local volunteer Doris Hanscombe. 

Moving to 2016, plans were progressing for a multi-million-pound heritage rail project based at Wolferton Station. The initiative saw the launch of a new steam locomotive, the Spirit of Sandringham, with the presentation of its official nameplates. These events highlight just a few of the community projects and historical reflections that have taken place in the region over the past decade.

stories.headline: West Norfolk Council defends swimming pool planning costs
stories.brief:
West Norfolk Council is considering spending over £845,000 on the planning stages for new swimming facilities at Lynnsport in King’s Lynn. Council leader Alistair Beales has defended the expenditure as proportionate, citing the high costs of planning in a flood zone and rising construction prices. The proposed project aims to replace the existing St James Swimming Pool, which is currently safe but described as deteriorating.

The Corporate Projects Panel has recommended that the cabinet approve the funding at their next meeting on September 8. However, the council has declined to provide a public breakdown of the costs or reveal the price of extending the life of the current facility. There is no guarantee the new pool will be built.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn Town fan fulfils final wish at The Walks
stories.brief:
A lifelong King’s Lynn Town supporter has fulfilled a final wish to watch his team play. Forty-three-year-old James Mason, who is battling a terminal illness, attended Monday’s National League North match against Scarborough Athletic at The Walks. 

Club officials and local supporters helped arrange the visit, which included a presentation of a signed shirt and match ball from players Aaron Jones and Tom Dickens. Mr Mason, who has followed the Linnets since his teenage years, was accompanied by family and friends. The family expressed their gratitude to the club, the hospice charity Tapping House, and Clenchwarton Cabs for providing the transport necessary to make the day possible.

stories.headline: Police appeal for information on wanted man Liam Clarke
stories.brief:
Norfolk Police are searching for 47-year-old Liam Clarke, who is also known as Liam Cook. Officers are looking for him after he failed to attend a scheduled hearing at Norwich Magistrates’ Court. Mr. Clarke is described as five feet nine inches tall with a thin build, short brown hair, and blue eyes. He has known connections to King’s Lynn, Swaffham, and Wisbech.

Anyone with information regarding his current whereabouts is urged to contact the police via their website or by calling the independent charity Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111. Please quote reference number 35/11070/26 when providing any details.

stories.headline: West Norfolk modellers raise over £2,300 for King’s Lynn Night Shelter
stories.brief:
Members of the West Norfolk International Plastic Modellers’ Society have donated more than £2,300 to the King’s Lynn Night Shelter. The funds were raised during the club’s annual model show held at the Littleport Leisure Centre in June, which attracted 19 traders and over 200 members of the public. 

The charity donation was presented to shelter representatives this past Wednesday. The club, which meets at the William Burt Social Club in West Winch, chooses a local charity to support each year. This latest contribution will assist the shelter, which does not receive government funding, in its ongoing work supporting the homeless across the region.

stories.headline: Queen Elizabeth Hospital addresses service closure concerns
stories.brief:
The Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn has issued a statement regarding the future of its services following reports of potential unit closures. The hospital trust confirms that no decisions have been made regarding the future of its Accident and Emergency, intensive care, or maternity departments. 

Officials state they are currently exploring long-term clinical strategies for the Norfolk and Waveney area, but have no preferred options at this stage. The trust says any future proposals for significant service changes would require robust clinical evidence, as well as formal staff and public consultation. The hospital is currently working to address operational challenges as part of a long-term plan for healthcare across the region.

stories.headline: Wisbech Town Council objects to new 24-hour adult gaming centre licence
stories.brief:
Wisbech Town Council has voted unanimously to formally object to a gambling licence application for a proposed 24-hour adult gaming centre at 28 Market Place. The site, a former Halifax Bank that closed in January, received planning permission for a change of use in June.

During Tuesday’s meeting, councillors expressed concerns regarding the potential impact on vulnerable residents, citing the venue's proximity to local support services. Members argued that a third gaming centre in the town could increase the risk of financial harm and acquisitive crime. The formal objection will now be submitted to Fenland District Council for consideration under the Gambling Act 2005.

stories.headline: Wisbech Library to close for five-week refurbishment
stories.brief:
Wisbech Library is set to close at the end of this month for a five-week period to allow for essential building upgrades. During the closure, the site on The Crescent will undergo a series of improvements, including the installation of new air conditioning. 

Further work will focus on the ground floor, where new carpets are to be fitted and a new children’s area will be created. The upcoming project was announced by Councillor Samantha Hoy during a Wisbech Town Council meeting held on Tuesday evening.

stories.headline: Wisbech Mayor reviews recent community engagements
stories.brief:
The Mayor of Wisbech, Councillor Lucie Foice-Beard, has provided an update on her recent community activities during Tuesday’s town council meeting. Over the past month, the Mayor attended several local events, including the town’s Rock Fest and the 150th Wisbech parkrun. She also visited the Wisbech Girls Venture Corps Cadets summer camp and participated in a 16-mile charity walk from Whittlesey to Wisbech to support the Alan Hudson Centre.

Looking ahead, Councillor Foice-Beard highlighted upcoming local events, including the Fenland Food Festival at the Queen Mary Centre this Saturday, Heritage weekends throughout September, and the return of the Wisbech funfair later this month.

stories.headline: Police report August activity in Wisbech
stories.brief:
Neighbourhood officers in Wisbech have reported on their efforts to address drug dealing and anti-social behaviour throughout August. During the month, police conducted 27 stop-searches and made 13 arrests. The operation also resulted in nine drug seizures, with five linked to suspected supply offences, alongside the seizure of three e-bikes and the granting of one partial closure order. Officers additionally filed 40 intelligence submissions while assisting other departments.

The force has invited residents to discuss local concerns at an online community meeting scheduled for 7pm on Tuesday, September 22. Police have thanked the public for sharing information, noting that community reports remain vital to their ongoing work in the town.

stories.headline: Off-road electric bike seized and rider arrested in Wisbech
stories.brief:
Police in Wisbech have seized an off-road electric bike and arrested its rider following a traffic stop on Nene Parade. Fenland response officers spotted the vehicle being driven at speed while they were attending an unrelated incident in the area. 

The rider was arrested on suspicion of driving offences, and the bike was subsequently confiscated. A police spokesperson reminded the public that operating these vehicles on public roads without proper registration, insurance, and a valid licence is illegal. Such offences can result in vehicle seizure, penalty points, and financial fines.

stories.headline: Possible closures of three key units at King’s Lynn’s Queen Elizabeth Hospital discussed
stories.brief:
Senior leaders at the Norfolk and Waveney University Hospitals Group are discussing the potential closure of accident and emergency, intensive care, and maternity units at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn. The hospital, which serves much of Fenland, is currently part of a long-term strategy review for the county’s three flagship hospitals. 

The group stated that no final decisions have been made and any changes would require public consultation. While the hospital is undergoing a £1.4 billion rebuild, local MPs have expressed differing views on the potential service changes. The hospital group maintains that patients in West Norfolk will continue to have access to urgent and emergency care services on-site.

stories.headline: Wisbech incinerator construction continues as planned
stories.brief:
Construction of the Wisbech incinerator is proceeding according to schedule, eleven months after work began. Current progress includes piling, drainage, and the installation of foundation slabs and walls for the main storage bunker. Two cranes, each approximately 50 metres high, are now visible on the site. Additionally, work has commenced to widen New Bridge Lane.

The Medworth team confirmed that construction will continue throughout the winter, with structural steel work expected to begin in late 2026. While the project faced significant opposition from local councils and campaign groups during the planning stages, including a failed High Court challenge by Fenland District Council, the construction team states that maintaining site cleanliness and keeping neighbours informed remains a priority.

stories.headline: Wisbech cinema announces ticket price cuts for National Cinema Day
stories.brief:
The Light Cinema in Wisbech is reducing ticket prices to £3 for all films throughout this coming weekend. The offer, which runs all day on both Saturday and Sunday, is being held to mark National Cinema Day. 

The schedule includes screenings of Cars, Coyote vs. ACME, and Insidious: Out of the Further, alongside a variety of other titles. Residents are encouraged to visit the cinema’s official website to view the full programme and further details regarding the promotion.
